text: Rahul: "It is difficult to fight against peer pressure. Youth easily gets influenced by the lifestyle of its peers." Radhika: "Peer pressure has its benefits as well. keyPoints: Reported speech shifts present tense to past: "gets" → "got"
Pronouns shift to third person: "us" → "them"
"our"/"its" adjust to match the reporting perspective

text: Read the conversation between two friends Ravi and Reena. Complete the sentence by reporting Reena's reply correctly. Ravi: "Reena, lend me hundred rupees." "will" shifts to "would" in reported speech
Pronouns shift: "I"/"you" → "she"/"him"; "right now" → "right then"

text: Report the dialogue between a mother and a daughter by completing the sentence: Mother: "Why are you looking so worried?" Daughter: "My exams are approaching." In response to the question of the mother, the daughter replied that ______. (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: her exams were approaching.
keyPoints: Present tense shifts to past: "are approaching" → "were approaching"
"My" shifts to "her" to match the reporting perspective
The reply is reported as a statement, not a question

text: Identify the error in the given sentence and supply the correction: "The ship Titanic and her fate continues to fascinate the imagination of the people." (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: Error: continues. Correction: continue. The subject is compound ("The ship Titanic and her fate" — two things), so it needs the plural verb "continue", not the singular "continues".
keyPoints: Subject is compound: "the ship Titanic" AND "her fate" — two things, so plural
A compound subject joined by "and" takes a plural verb
Error: continues → Correction: continue

text: Ritu and Randeep are talking. Report Ritu's question: Ritu: "Where are you going?" Ritu asked ________. (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: Ritu asked Randeep where he was going.
keyPoints: A reported wh-question keeps the question word ("where") but drops the question format/mark
Present tense shifts to past: "are going" → "was going"
Pronoun shifts: "you" → "he"

text: Identify the error in the newspaper headline and supply the correction: "Attractive packages for different Tourist destination – Mizoram, Kashmir, Kerala, Goa." (2023 Board)

keyPoints: Four destinations are named, so the noun must be plural
"Different" signals more than one, requiring a plural noun
Error: destination → Correction: destinations

text: Fill in the blank by using the correct form of the word in the bracket, for a portion of a letter: "Dear Sir, In response to your query, the document that ______ (explain) our country's sustainability initiatives has been attached for your consideration." (2024 Board)
modelAnswer: explains
keyPoints: The relative clause "that ___ our sustainability initiatives" describes a singular noun, "the document"
A singular subject in the present tense takes the -s form: "explains"
The main clause ("has been attached") stays present perfect; the relative clause stays simple present

text: Read the given sentence, identify the error and supply the correction: "The uniquely flavoured dish was interestingly enough to captivate my taste buds." (2024 Board)

Adverbs (-ly forms) modify verbs; adjectives describe nouns
Error: interestingly → Correction: interesting

text: Raashi and Ratul had a conversation about volunteer work. Report Raashi's question: Raashi: "What challenges have you faced while volunteering?" (2024 Board)

keyPoints: The question word "what" is retained, but word order becomes statement-like
Present perfect shifts to past perfect: "have faced" → "had faced"
Pronoun shifts: "you" → "he"

text: Identify the error and supply correction for the given sentence from an e-commerce website's return policy: "We offers a 30-day return policy on all unopened products purchased from our websites." (2024 Board)
modelAnswer: Error: offers. Correction: offer. The subject "We" is plural/first-person, so the verb must not take the third-person singular -s ending: "We offer".
keyPoints: "We" is a first-person plural pronoun
First-person and plural subjects don't take the -s verb ending
Error: offers → Correction: offer

text: Report the dialogue between a vendor and his customer, by completing the sentence: Vendor: "You look a little different today!" Customer: "Yes, I just got a new haircut." Pronoun shifts: "I" → "he"
"Just" is retained to show the recency of the action

keyPoints: "Aim" is followed by the preposition "at", not "in"
"Aimed at" is followed by a gerund ("increasing"), not the bare verb "increase"
Error: in → Correction: at (with "increase" becoming "increasing")

text: Fill in the blank by using the correct form of the word in the brackets, for the given portion of a letter: 'Thank you for _________ (consider) my application. I look forward to working in your organization.' (2025 Board)
modelAnswer: considering
keyPoints: "Thank you for" is followed by a gerund (-ing form), not a bare verb
"Consider" becomes "considering"
This is a fixed pattern: preposition "for" + gerund

text: Read the given sentence, identify the error and supply the correction: "Ninety-seven percent of the Earth's water is salty ocean water and another two percent is trapping in the Earth's ice caps and glaciers." (2025 Board)
modelAnswer: Error: trapping. Correction: trapped. The water is acted upon (it is trapped by the ice), so the passive past participle "trapped" is needed, not the active/continuous "trapping".
keyPoints: The water doesn't trap itself — it is trapped (passive voice)
"Is trapping" (active/continuous) should be "is trapped" (passive, a state)
Error: trapping → Correction: trapped

text: Yukti and Sanjay had a conversation about going to a restaurant. Report Yukti's question: "Does this restaurant serve good South Indian food?" (2025 Board)
modelAnswer: Yukti asked Sanjay if/whether that restaurant served good South Indian food.
keyPoints: A reported yes/no question uses "if" or "whether"
Present tense shifts to past: "does...serve" → "served"
"this" shifts to "that" as it moves away from the speaker's immediate context

text: Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option, to complete the sentence taken from a book about 'Birds': Each year, thousands of birds __________ (migrate/immigrate/emigrate) southwards to avoid the harsh winter, embarking on an incredible journey that spans thousands of miles. (2025 Board)
modelAnswer: migrate. "Migrate" means to move seasonally between regions (as birds do); "immigrate" means to move INTO a country to live there permanently, and "emigrate" means to move OUT of one's own country permanently — neither fits a seasonal, round-trip movement.
keyPoints: "Migrate" = seasonal movement between places (fits birds moving south for winter)
"Immigrate"/"emigrate" describe permanent movement into/out of a country, not seasonal travel
Correct word: migrate

text: Identify and correct the error in the given line taken from an agency's advertisement: "Tell us much about your project and we'll select suitable candidates for you to hire." (2025 Board)
modelAnswer: Error: much. Correction: more. In an affirmative imperative sentence like this, "more" is the natural comparative/quantity word; "much" is typically used in questions or negative sentences, not plain affirmative requests like this one.
keyPoints: "Much" is normally used in questions/negatives, not plain affirmative statements
"Tell us more" is the natural, idiomatic phrasing here
Error: much → Correction: more

text: Report the dialogue between two friends by completing the sentence: Bhawna: "I finished the project yesterday." Sohail: "That's great! Are you going to present it tomorrow?" modelAnswer: she had finished the project the day before.
keyPoints: Simple past shifts to past perfect: "finished" → "had finished"
"Yesterday" shifts to "the day before" since the reporting happens later
Pronoun shifts: "I" → "she"

text: Identify and correct the error in the given note in an air purifier's instruction manual: "The plug should fit upto the outlet. If it doesn't fit, do not force it in." (2025 Board)

"Upto" describes reaching a limit/extent, which doesn't match the meaning here

The base verb form follows "to" in an infinitive: identify, not identifying
Error: identifying → Correction: identify

"Tomorrow" shifts to "the next day" since the report happens later

keyPoints: The subject is "the members" (plural), not "the jury" alone
A plural subject takes the plural verb "are"

text: How, according to Buddha, can one obtain peace of mind? (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: According to the Buddha, one obtains peace of mind by giving up craving and desire, and by accepting that suffering, loss and death are universal parts of life that no one can escape. Once a person stops clinging to what cannot last, their mind can find peace.
keyPoints: Peace of mind comes from giving up craving/desire
One must accept the impermanence and universality of suffering and death
Clinging to what cannot last is the root cause of sorrow

keyPoints: Lomov is a hypochondriac, obsessively anxious about his health
He is timid/indecisive about proposing marriage, motivated partly by property (Oxen Meadows)
He is easily provoked into quarrels over trivial disagreements, a source of comedy

text: What are the essential qualities for becoming a scientist, according to the chapter 'The Making of a Scientist'? (2022 Board)

Patience, persistence and hard work in research
Courage to question and learn independently, undeterred by setbacks

text: Describe the feelings of the young lawyer when he came to know the reality of the hack driver. (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: The young lawyer felt shocked and embarrassed on realising that the friendly hack driver he had trusted and confided in was, in fact, Oliver Lutkins himself — the very man he had been sent to serve legal papers on. At the same time, he felt a grudging admiration for how cleverly and thoroughly he had been outwitted.
keyPoints: Shock and embarrassment at realising the hack driver deceived him
The hack driver was Oliver Lutkins himself, the man he was sent to find
Also felt a reluctant admiration for how cleverly he was tricked

text: What attracts visitors to Coorg? (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: Visitors are drawn to Coorg's evergreen forests, rolling hills, coffee and spice plantations, and its cool, invigorating climate. Its unique culture — the brave, hospitable Kodava people, permitted to carry firearms without a licence — and adventure activities like river rafting and trekking, along with the sacred Talacauvery (source of the river Cauvery), are also major attractions.
keyPoints: Evergreen forests, hills, coffee/spice plantations and a pleasant climate
The distinctive culture and hospitality of the Kodava people
Adventure sports (rafting, trekking) and the sacred Talacauvery source of the Cauvery

text: Matilda realised that one little act of negligence can lead to total ruin. What do you learn from this and how would you move on in life? (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: From Matilda's story, one learns that contentment and honesty matter more than pride and the pursuit of appearances. A single moment of carelessness (losing the borrowed necklace, and not admitting it honestly right away) led to ten years of hardship that could have been avoided. In life, one should be honest about mistakes immediately, live within one's means, and value what one has rather than envying what one lacks.
keyPoints: A small act of carelessness/pride caused years of unnecessary suffering
Lesson: be honest immediately about mistakes rather than concealing them out of pride
Lesson: be content with what one has, rather than living beyond one's means for appearances

text: Valli was a mature girl and ahead of her age. Justify the statement with evidence from the text. (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: Valli shows maturity beyond her years through her careful, patient planning — saving small amounts of money and quietly gathering details about bus timings and fares in advance. Her sharp observation and curiosity about the world around her, and her calm, practical reaction to seeing a dead cow on the road (reasoning through it rather than reacting emotionally like a typical child), further reveal her maturity. Undertaking the bus journey alone, without adult help, also shows her self-reliance and confidence.
keyPoints: Careful, patient planning and saving money in advance for the trip
Calm, practical (not overly emotional) reaction to the dead cow, showing mature reasoning
Self-reliance in undertaking the journey alone, without adult help

text: What did Pranjol and Rajvir do during the journey? Why? (Glimpses of India — Tea from Assam) (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: During the train journey, Pranjol slept for most of the way, while Rajvir stayed awake, eagerly looking out of the window at the passing countryside. Rajvir was excited and curious because this was his first visit to Assam and a tea garden, whereas Pranjol, having grown up there, had seen it all before and felt no novelty in it.
keyPoints: Pranjol slept through most of the journey; Rajvir stayed awake, watching eagerly
Rajvir was excited as it was his first visit to Assam/a tea garden
Pranjol, being from there, found nothing new or exciting about the familiar landscape

text: Who read the letter sent by Lencho? What did he do then? (2023 Board)

Touched and amused by Lencho's simple, unwavering faith, he decided to help by collecting money from himself, his employees, and friends — though he could only gather about seventy pesos. He sent this money to Lencho in an envelope, signed "God", to keep Lencho's faith alive.
keyPoints: The postmaster read Lencho's letter to God
Moved by Lencho's faith, he collected money from himself and others
He sent the money to Lencho signed as "God", though it fell short of the full amount

text: Where is Coorg located? Write any two characteristics of the people of Coorg. (2023 Board)

Its people, the Kodavas, are known for their martial traditions and courage (they are the only Indian community permitted to carry firearms without a licence) and for their warm hospitality towards visitors.
keyPoints: Coorg is in Karnataka, between Mysore and Mangalore
The Kodava people have a strong martial/warrior tradition (permitted firearms without licence)
The Kodavas are also known for their hospitality

chapter: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
text: How does the poem 'The Tale of Custard the Dragon' differ from the traditional ballad? (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: Traditional ballads typically narrate serious, tragic tales of heroism in a solemn tone. This poem instead uses a light-hearted, humorous, mock-heroic style — the seemingly cowardly dragon Custard turns out to be the real hero when danger strikes, subverting the reader's expectations. Its playful rhyme, comic exaggeration, and gentle irony replace the gravity typical of a traditional ballad.
keyPoints: Traditional ballads are serious/tragic in tone; this poem is humorous and light-hearted
It subverts expectations: the "cowardly" dragon becomes the true hero (mock-heroic twist)
Playful rhyme and comic exaggeration replace the solemnity of a typical ballad

text: What does the Buddha say about the world? (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: The Buddha says that the world is full of sorrow and suffering, and this suffering arises from craving and attachment to things that cannot last. Nothing in the world is permanent, and death comes to everyone without exception. To be freed from grief, one must overcome desire and accept the impermanence of all things.
keyPoints: The world is full of sorrow, arising from craving/attachment
Nothing in the world is permanent; death is universal, sparing no one
Freedom from grief comes from giving up desire and accepting impermanence

text: Why does Anil not hand over Hari Singh to the police? (2023 Board)

He trusted Hari Singh and believed he deserved a chance to reform — especially since Hari Singh himself felt guilty and returned the stolen money. Anil valued this trust and the possibility of change over punishing him.
keyPoints: Anil already knew about the theft but chose to trust Hari Singh instead of punishing him
He believed Hari Singh could reform and deserved a chance
Hari Singh's own guilt and return of the money justified Anil's trust

text: What opinion did Mr. Weiherer, Ebright's Social Science teacher, have about him? (2023 Board)

keyPoints: Weiherer considered Ebright the best student of his long teaching career
He admired Ebright's exceptional curiosity and inquisitive mind
He noted Ebright's drive for independent, serious research beyond normal school expectations

keyPoints: Herriot advised a strict, controlled diet (no titbits) and regular exercise for Tricki
This was needed because Tricki was overfed and unwell due to overindulgence
Mrs. Pumphrey reluctantly agreed, and Tricki recovered under Herriot's care

keyPoints: She saved money gradually and gathered information about routes/fares beforehand
She waited patiently for the right opportunity
She boarded the bus alone, in secret, showing determination and self-reliance

text: Through the story of Kisa Gotami, what did the Buddha try to preach to the common man? (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: Through Kisa Gotami — who lost her only child and sought a cure for death — the Buddha taught that death and grief are universal; there is no household untouched by loss. By asking her to find a house that had never known death, he showed her (and all people) that suffering is inherent to life and cannot be escaped, so one must accept impermanence rather than cling to grief.
keyPoints: Kisa Gotami sought a way to bring her dead child back to life
The Buddha sent her to find a house untouched by death — she found none
Lesson: death and sorrow are universal; everyone must accept impermanence

text: Education is always a great asset in the life of a woman. How did Bholi, an educated girl, face the challenge posed by Bishamber's greed? (2023 Board)

keyPoints: Bishamber demanded extra dowry just before the wedding, revealing his greed
Bholi's education gave her the confidence and self-respect to refuse the marriage herself
She chose independence (becoming a teacher) over marrying a greedy man

text: Those who are satisfied with what they have are happy in life. Those who aspire more than what they can afford ruin their life. Matilda was one such person. If she were content with her life she would have led a happy life. Elaborate on the basis of the chapter 'The Necklace.' (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: Matilda was never satisfied with her modest, middle-class life and constantly yearned for wealth and luxury beyond her means. To appear glamorous at a party, she borrowed a necklace, which she then lost. Rather than admit this honestly, she and her husband borrowed heavily to replace it, condemning themselves to ten years of poverty and hard labour to repay the debt — only to learn afterwards that the original necklace was artificial and worth very little. Had Matilda been content with her situation, none of this suffering would have occurred.
keyPoints: Matilda's constant discontent with her modest life drove her to borrow a necklace for appearances
Losing it led her and her husband into ten years of debt and hardship to replace it
The final twist (the necklace was fake) shows how her discontent caused needless suffering

He sensed being part of something that would be remembered for generations

text: Explain why the speaker mentions God in the poem 'For Anne Gregory'. (2024 Board)

This highlights how shallow, appearance-based human love is compared to unconditional, essence-based divine love.
keyPoints: Young men love Anne only for her physical beauty (yellow hair)
The speaker says only God could love her for her true, inner self

text: What message might the Buddha's story hold for those who are in positions of power and privilege? (2024 Board)

keyPoints: A small, simple act of nature (snow dust falling from a crow) changes the poet's mood
